guide.title: Xul's Overview
guide.text:
Xul is a high damage Bruiser that abuses his strong
AoE damage from his abilities to quickly clear
any minion wave, which then allows him to create many Skeletal Warriors thanks to
Raise Skeleton, letting him become a major threat to towers
and, by extension, making the wave much harder to clear.
Xul also excels against melee compositions, given he can easily land
Cursed Strikes into many targets, reducing their attack speed
and making him really hard to deal without crowd control.

guide.title: Xul's Strengths and Weaknesses
guide.text:
Strengths
Exceptional waveclear
Excellent AoE damage
Decent self-sustain thanks to Bone Armor and Harvest Vitality
Mortal Wound counters healing abilities
Good crowd control for team to follow up thanks to Bone Prison
Able to apply lots of debuffs on attack speed, damage, healing and armor
Weaknesses
Very susceptible to crowd control
Weak against compositions featuring many ranged or poke-centric heroes
Really hard to play when facing counters
Susceptible to gank attempts
Requires good positioning

guide.title: Xul's Synergies and Counters
guide.text:
Xul synergizes with
Xul sinergizes very well with Heroes that are able to protect him while he receives burst
damage or crowd control like Medivh. He also excels with good
follow up for Bone Prison, like
Tyrande with Lunar Flare,
Falstad with Hinterland Blast
or Li-Ming with all her Abilities.
Xul is countered by
Due to not having mobility,
Xul suffers a lot from displacement effects
or crowd control in general,
making Heroes such as E.T.C.
huge threats, while Johanna is able to Blind
him during Cursed Strikes, reducing his effectiveness.
Xul also struggles against Heroes with long range or with high burst damage that allows
them to follow up the crowd control, like Jaina
and Sgt. Hammer.

guide.title: Xul's Maps
guide.text:
Xul's stronger maps
Xul's average maps
Xul's weaker maps
Xul shines in maps with nearby lanes, as he will be able to easily abuse his
waveclear and Skeletal Warriors, making him excellent on
Blackheart's Bay, Tomb of the Spider Queen, and Infernal Shrines. He will also be decent
on big maps where the Objective will be very time consuming, allowing him to get
a great experience lead through split-pushing, like
in Sky Temple, Garden of Terror, or Cursed Hollow.
However, Xul does not perform as well in 2-lane maps, given he cannot abuse his
fast waveclear to spawn skeletons and go to another lane, which he normally would
in a bigger map.

guide.title: Xul's Tips and Tricks
guide.text:
Cursed Strikes is one of the best waveclear Abilities in the game, so you should always be attempting to clear a wave and instantly Mount up and rotate to another lane, getting maximum value out of Raise Skeleton.
Since Xul does not have a strong early game, sometimes it is better to (in some maps) avoid fighting for the first Objective (Infernal Shrines and Cursed Hollow can be good examples), and instead proceed to the opposite lane in order to split-push between the other 2 lanes. A good practice is to warn your team before doing this, given they will be having a numerical disadvantage in the fight, and will have to play it safe.
Keep in mind Xul has limited mobility, so during fights it is a good idea to wait for your tank to engage, or for enemy heroes to spend their crowd control before going in, given you will struggle to enter and escape fights.
A good way to use Bone Prison is on a tank just after they spent their defensive skills, a Johanna without Iron Skin or an Anub'arak without Burrow Charge often turn out to be an easy kill, given they will be rooted in the same place for 2 seconds.
Since Bone Prison has a tiny range, it is recommended to always stay mounted so you can easily find a way to engage your desired target.
See our Abilities page for further information »

guide.title: Xul's Role in the Current Meta
guide.text:
Each minion wave spawns every 30 seconds (starting from 00:00); this has the
same cooldown as Bone Armor, which allows you to ignore the
enemy Bruiser every time you step up to clear the wave. Thanks to this, Xul will
always be ahead of his enemies, enabling him to move towards the closest lane to
either gank or clear it.
Since Xul is slightly dependent on talents to be really impactful in fights, it
is better to focus on clearing waves between two lanes during the early game.
After you get your main talent for the build ( Harvest Vitality
for Cursed Strikes Build, Amplify Damage for Bone Prison Build, and
Decrepify for Spectral Scythe Build) start looking for
fights—Xul will be extremely good in them.

abilities.title: Raise Skeleton
abilities.text:
Raise Skeleton
(D)
Xul
When a nearby enemy Minion dies, it becomes a Skeletal Warrior with 240 (+4% per level) Health that attacks for 21 (+4% per level) damage and lasts up to 12 seconds. Upon death, Skeletal Warriors deal 40 (+4% per level) damage to nearby enemies. Up to 3 Skeletal Warriors can be active at once when spawned in this way.
Xul's trait will not only increase his pushing capabilities greatly, but will
also greatly increase his damage in fights.
Up to 3 Skeletal Warriors can be active at once, and every extra Summon evoked
will make the first spawned to explode dealing 40 damage to enemies, allowing
you to deal decent damage into the opposing laner by just hitting the wave.
If the enemy is far from your warriors, you can use Bone Prison
to make skeletons move towards them to guarantee the explosion damage
while clearing the other Minions.

abilities.title: Bone Armor
abilities.text:
Bone Armor
(1)
Xul
Activate to gain a Shield equal to 25% of Xul's maximum Health for 3 seconds.
Bone Armor can help Xul a lot when facing opposing laner,
since he can use it to ignore the damage received while clearing the wave. This
is a recommended tactic when you are having trouble rotating faster, but be aware that the
Shield is your main way to survive ganks. Only use it in the wave if you are sure
that you will not get ganked soon.
After getting Harvest Vitality, Xul will have a lot of
self-healing in fights. It is better to only use Bone Armor
when you are below
70% Health to not lose value from healing. If the opposing team features a lot of
crowd control or burst damage, the Shield should be
used early on to prevent you from dying during a Stun or Silence.
Bone Armor will be a whole different skill depending of Xul's Level 1 Talent.
The differences and how it should be used will be mentioned
in the Talent Build page.

abilities.title: Spectral Scythe
abilities.text:
Spectral Scythe
(Q)
Xul
Mana: 55
Cooldown: 8 seconds
Summon a scythe that travels to Xul after 1 second, dealing 190 (+4% per level) damage to enemies and spawning a Skeletal Warrior when hitting enemy Heroes. These do not count towards Xul's Raise Skeleton maximum.
Spectral Scythe causes Xul to summon a scythe to the target
location that travels back to him after 1 second, dealing a large amount of damage
to all enemies in its path.
Xul's waveclear becomes even more powerful
if he uses Spectral Scythe effectively, which usually requires him to
place the scythse behind enemy Archer Minions.
Aiming and landing Spectral Scythe can sometimes be tricky, especially against moving
enemy targets. Consequently, it is often recommended to wait until you have
successfully Rooted someone by using Bone Prison and then
following up with Spectral Scythe on the imprisoned target.
After getting Mortal Wound at 20, it is recommended to only
use against someone with low life or affected by some crowd control,
considering the healing reduction will be much more useful than the damage.

abilities.title: Cursed Strikes
abilities.text:
Cursed Strikes
(W)
Xul
Passive
Xul's Basic Attacks deal damage in a wide area and reduce the Attack Speed of Heroes and Summons by 40% for 2 seconds. Lasts 4 seconds once triggered.
Cursed Strikes will make all your attacks for the next 4
seconds cleave. 5 attacks can be landed in the duration, so it is crucial to hit
all of them. If your enemy starts running from you after you activate it, keep
walking towards them while stopping to attack the closest Minion or Hero every
time you can, so your cleave will hit them even when they are outside of your Attack range.
During team fights, Cursed Strikes should be used against Attack Speed dependent
Heroes, such as Illidan, Thrall, or Kharazim, in order to cripple their combat
efficiency. When getting ganked, Xul can deny a considerable part of the damage
by landing some Cursed Strikes attacks while walking backwards, reducing their
Attack Speed.

abilities.title: Bone Prison
abilities.text:
Bone Prison
(E)
Xul
Mana: 70
Cooldown: 10 seconds
After a 2 second delay, deal 80 (+4% per level) damage and Root the target enemy Hero for 1.75 seconds. All nearby Skeletal Warriors will fixate on the target for their duration.
Bone Prison is an incredibly powerful crowd control
Ability for two major reasons. Firstly, its 2-second Root effect provides enough
time for Xul and the rest of his team to approach the affected enemy target and
damage it. Secondly, Bone Prison comes with flashy visual effect that marks the
chosen enemy, which clearly signalises your allies which target to focus while it also
causes all of your active Skeletons to fixate on the Rooted target for additional damage.
A good way to use Bone Prison is on a Tank just after they
spent their defensive skills. Johanna
without Iron Skin or an
Anub'arak without Burrow Charge
often turn out to be an easy kill, given they will be Rooted in the same place for
2 seconds.

abilities.title: Poison Nova
abilities.text:
In this section we discuss how this Heroic Ability works and give some tips on how to use it.
If you are looking for a detailed explanation on when and why you should pick it,
check out the dedicated section in the Talent Build page.
Poison Nova
(R)
Xul
Heroic
Mana: 100
Cooldown: 90 seconds
After 0.5 seconds, release poisonous missiles that deal 630 (+4% per level) damage to all enemies hit over 10 seconds.
Poison Nova is an incredibly strong Heroic Ability that deals
almost half the life of a Hanzo or a
Valla. However, that damage will be dealt
over 10 seconds, thus allowing Healers to easily save the dying target. It is also
easy to avoid when you are not close to Xul. Therefore, Poison Nova is a really
good option when either facing a composition with many melee Heroes, or against
Healers incapable of supporting all their team,
as they only have single-target healing (such as Lt. Morales).
Using Poison Nova right at the start of a fight might not be a good idea,
since it will be easily dodged by the ranged opposing Heroes. It is recommended
to wait a couple seconds after fight starts to use it, complicating for enemy Heroes
without mobility tools (for example Kael'thas)
to dodge it, as they might be focused on other things in the combat.

abilities.title: Skeletal Mages
abilities.text:
In this section we discuss how this Heroic Ability works and give some tips on how to use it.
If you are looking for a detailed explanation on when and why you should pick it,
check out the dedicated section in the Talent Build page.
Skeletal Mages
(R)
Xul
Heroic
Mana: 80
Cooldown: 90 seconds
Summon 4 Frost Mages in a line that attack nearby enemies for 47 (+4% per level) damage a second and Slow them by 30% for 2 seconds. Last up to 15 seconds.
Skeletal Mages is a great tool to zone
enemy Heroes and Slow them down. The efficiency of Skeletal Mages can
be increased even further if your team has decent crowd control Abilities, which
enable you to follow up extremely well on targets already Slowed by Skeletal
Mages.
Skeletal Mages is a crucial Heroic Ability when you are having trouble
getting close to ranged Heroes, as the Slow will enable you to reach them.
Due to the relatively long cooldown on Skeletal Mages, it should be cast with
caution. Use narrow choke points and
impassable terrain to your advantage in order to successfully trap enemy
high-priority targets.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Backlash is your standard choice, which requires you to
stay close to nearby enemy Heroes in order to benefit from its effect. The damage
will still be dealt even if the Shield is broken before running out. In most
scenarios, it will have more value on melee Heroes who are easier to hit
and tend to have higher maximum Health.
Shackler in a Cursed Strikes Build might refund Bone Armor's
Cooldown several times in a fight. To do so, Xul has to be free to hit several attacks
without any concerns in a fight. If this happens, you would probably win the combat
with any other Talent, placing this Talent slightly behind the other two.
Shade comes with the drawback of increasing
Bone Armor's cooldown by 10 seconds. However, the Basic
Attack evasion is capable of absorbing more damage done to Xul than the
original Shield of Bone Armor, especially against hard-hitting Assassins like
Thrall or Greymane. Shade is the best Talent against
more than one Hero heavily focused on Basic Attacks.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Since Spectral Scythe's damage cannot compare to the extra
damage provided by the 2 Skeletons spawnwed by Jailors,
Reaper's Toll is not recommended on any build.
Grim Scythe lays a solid foundation for a Cursed Strikes Build.
Its cooldown reduction is vital to increasing the value of follow up Talents like
Harvest Vitality at Level 7 and Rapid Harvest at Level 13, as it allows
you to use Cursed Strikes with all of its self-healing and Attack Speed buffs.
Jailors's Quest reward can be completed quite easily if Xul rotates between
multiple lanes in order to raise as many Skeletons as possible. It is a good Talent
in a Bone Prison Build, since it will slightly increase your burst damage.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Harvest Vitality is vital in a Cursed Strikes build.
It also works very well in other builds and should be the choice if Xul is having
troubles facing the enemy laner, since you can ignore him due to the 70% self-Heal.
Trag'Oul's Essence provides almost no self-sustain in fights.
The Mana provided is way too low and not necessary, since you do not need to
use any Ability other than Cursed Strikes to clear the wave after Level 9. However,
The small self-sustain provided by it is very good in small skirmishes that happen between you and the opposing
Offlaner, being a good option if you do not need the other Talents.
Wall Of Bones is a really strong Talent against compositions
with much burst damage in the form of Spell Damage.
It should not be picked in a Cursed Strikes Build,
since Harvest Vitality is necessary, but it is very impactful in the other builds,
since it increases your survivability considerably.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
In this section we discuss when and why to pick a given Heroic Ability.
If you want to read how they work in detail and/or you are looking for some tips on how to use them,
check them out on the Abilities and Strategy page.
Poison Nova is a powerful
area of effect damage over time Heroic
Ability, which becomes particularly powerful if the enemy team lacks
area of effect protection (healing, Shielding, or Armor).
Furthermore, melee Heroes obviously have a harder time dodging the Poison Nova's
projectiles, since Xul can reach them more easily than ranged Heroes. Consequently,
it is crucial to analyse the enemy team composition before picking Poison
Nova.
Skeletal Mages fulfills a different role
than Poison Nova, since it is less about dealing damage and more about
zoning. The wall of Skeletal Mages functions very similarly
to Tassadar's Force Wall,
it can either be used to prevent enemies from entering a specific area or it can
be used to chase down retreating opponents.

talent_pages.title: Level 13 Talents for Xul
talent_pages.text:
✓
Echoes of Death
(Level 13)
Xul
Spectral Scythe spawns 2 additional scythes next to the first after 1.5 seconds, dealing 40% damage.
?
Rapid Harvest
(Level 13)
Xul
Gain 5% Attack Speed for 3 seconds each time Cursed Strikes hits an enemy, up to 75%.
?
Amplify Damage
(Level 13)
Xul
Increase the Root duration of Bone Prison by 0.25 seconds. Enemies Rooted by Bone Prison lose 25 Armor for 2 seconds.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Echoes of Death offers increased waveclear
and area of effect damage,
which will greatly enhance Xul's combat performance during team fights. This Talent
also has good synergy with other Spectral Scythe-related Talents,
aggregating to a Spectral Scythe Build.
Rapid Harvest's Attack Speed bonus causes you to gain
more value from the cooldown and healing provided by
Grim Scythe and Harvest Vitality. As such,
we definitely recommend going for this Talent if you decided to commit to
a Cursed Strikes Build.
Amplify Damage enables Xul and his teammates to focus and
kill a single enemy Hero more efficiently by increasing all damage dealt by 25%.
It is crucial in a Bone Prison Build, but can still be picked in all the other builds.
Go for it if you have Heroes with high burst to kill the desired target
while Rooted (such as Li-Ming).

talent_pages.title: Level 16 Talents for Xul
talent_pages.text:
✓
Decrepify
(Level 16)
Xul
Enemy Heroes that are damaged by Spectral Scythe or Skeletal Warriors are Slowed by 30% for 2.5 seconds.
?
Weaken
(Level 16)
Xul
Enemy Heroes who are damaged by Cursed Strikes or Skeletal Warriors deal 35% less damage for 3 seconds.
?
Bone Spear
(Level 16)
Xul
Cooldown: 12 seconds
Deal 230 (+4% per level) damage to enemies in a line.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Decrepify is a major improvement to a Spectral Scythe Build, since
it will not only boost your engage and chase capabilities, but will also help at
hitting the secondary Scythes from Echoes of Death.
This Slow is reapplied by the
summoned Skeletal Warriors from the scythe.
Weaken will give a Cursed Strikes Build much more survivability,
considering that damage reduction will consequently make your Shield and healing better,
since it will sustain more attacks. With this Talent, remember to use Cursed Strikes
to protect your teammates as well. For example, it can be used on a
Kael'thas
while his Pyroblast is coming towards your teammates
in order to reduce the damage.
Bone Spear comes with a very short cooldown, therefore, it
will increase both Xul's burst and
sustained damage. Bone Spear should be used
when cleaning waves, since it will be up for fight and has no Mana cost.
In fights, it is better to use it when a target is Rooted
or Stunned, by either
your Bone Prison or friendly crowd control.

talent_pages.title: Level 20 Talents for Xul
talent_pages.text:
?
Andariel's Visage
(Level 20)
Xul
Poison Nova heals for 50% of the damage dealt and its duration is increased by 50%.
✘︎
Cold Hand of Death
(Level 20)
Xul
Increase the Slow of Frost Mages by 20%.
Every 5th Spectral Scythe that hits enemy Heroes spawns a Frost Mage instead of a Skeletal Warrior at their location.
✓
Mortal Wound
(Level 20)
Xul
Enemy Heroes hit by Spectral Scythe receive 75% less healing for 4 seconds.
✘︎
Kalan's Edict
(Level 20)
Xul
Each time Skeletal Warriors deal damage, reduce the cooldown of Bone Armor and Xul's Heroic Ability by 1.5%.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Andariel's Visage adds a significant amount of self-heal and damage to Xul's kit.
Poison Nova will heal from all targets hit, counting Structures, Minions, Heroes,
Summons, or Monsters. Therefore it should be used trying to hit the most targets it can.
The heal might make Xul almost immortal when paired with defensive Talents,
such as Harvest Vitality and Weaken.
This Talent is even better with a Cursed Strikes Build, considering it will allow you
to be in the middle of the fight in order to deal damage.
Cold Hand of Death is a very underwhelming choice.
Mostly the Slow increase in Frost Mages will not be necessary and the one created
from Scythe is irrelevant in fights. Most of the time, this Talent will be
overshadowed by Mortal Wound.
With Mortal Wound, Xul can turn many fights around by
reducing the effectiveness of healing Abilities, like Ancestral Healing
or Ray of Heaven, allowing his team to confirm the kill on a target.
This Talent is excellent in a Spectral Scythe Build, considering it can reduce almost
permanently the healing of every enemy Hero. Mortal Wound can be taken in any
of the other Builds, since the Healing reduction will be impactful in every game
against one or more Healers.
Kalan's Edict significantly lowers the cooldown of Xul's
Heroic Abilities whenever a Skeleton deals damage with a Basic Attack, which
unfortunately is a pretty underwhelming investment as you will already have your
Heroic Abilities ready in all the late game fights with or without this Talent.
To refund the Heroic Ability's cooldown completely in a fight, Skeletal Warriors
have to hit enemies at least 50 times, which is extremely hard to happen.
